stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Average Tempo in Recordings of Brandt's Violin Sonata (beats per minute)
Movement | Recorded 1930–1959 | Recorded 1990–2019
I (Allegro) | 132 | 144
II (Adagio) | 44 | 60
III (Rondo) | 152 | 156

Musicologist Rafael Okafor timed forty commercial recordings of Ottilie Brandt's 1887 Violin Sonata. Half were made between 1930 and 1959, and half between 1990 and 2019. Later performers, he observes, sped up every movement, but the change was largest in the slow Adagio. Okafor concludes that modern players treat the Adagio as singing rather than mourning: in the recent recordings, the movement averages ______ beats per minute.
explanation: The statement asks about the Adagio in the recent recordings. Find row II (Adagio), go across to the 1990–2019 column, and you get 60 beats per minute.

A.why: You worked out how much the Adagio sped up (60 − 44 = 16). The statement asks for the tempo the recent recordings average, not the size of the change.

B.why: You read the correct row but the wrong column. 44 is the Adagio's tempo in the 1930–1959 recordings, not the recent ones.

D.why: You read the correct column but the neighbouring row. 144 is the Allegro's tempo in the 1990–2019 recordings, not the Adagio's.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: Archaeologist Ines Calloway examined linen fragments from five medieval sites in a single river valley. Brisk Ford, at the river mouth, was a busy seaport where imported cloth was common. Arnhal, Coldwater, Dunmere, and Eskby lay inland. Calloway argues that fine weaving was not limited to the port. As evidence, she notes that among the inland sites, fragments from ______ had the highest average thread density.

figure.caption: Average Thread Density of Linen Fragments by Site
figure.alt: Bar graph of average threads per centimeter in linen fragments from five sites: Arnhal, Brisk Ford, Coldwater, Dunmere and Eskby.

explanation: The phrase "among the inland sites" leaves out Brisk Ford. Of the four inland bars, Dunmere's is tallest at 32 threads per centimeter, so Dunmere completes the statement.

A.why: You took the bar next to the right one. Arnhal's fragments average 28 threads per centimeter, which is below Dunmere's 32, so Arnhal is not the densest inland site.

B.why: You picked the tallest bar on the whole graph and ignored the words "among the inland sites." The passage says Brisk Ford was the seaport, so it is outside the group the statement asks about.

D.why: You reversed the comparison. Eskby has the lowest thread density of any site, not the highest among the inland ones.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Workers Holding Two or More Jobs (% of industry workforce)
Year | Retail | Transportation
2004 | 9 | 6
2008 | 11 | 8
2012 | 12 | 10
2016 | 12 | 13
2020 | 13 | 15

Labor economist Mira Szabo tracked the share of workers holding more than one job in two industries. App-based delivery work spread quickly during the 2010s. Szabo hypothesizes that it drew transportation workers into second jobs at higher rates than before. Consistent with this, she notes that the rate for transportation workers first rose above 10 percent in ______.
explanation: Go down the Transportation column and find the first value greater than 10. The figure for 2012 is exactly 10, which does not exceed 10. The next row, 2016, shows 13. The rate therefore first rose above 10 percent in 2016.

A.why: You read the Retail column. Retail first rose above 10 percent in 2008, but the statement is about transportation workers, whose rate that year was only 8 percent.

B.why: You treated reaching 10 percent as rising above it. In 2012 the transportation rate was exactly 10, so it had not yet gone past 10 percent.

D.why: 2020 is when the transportation rate was highest. The statement asks when it first went above 10 percent, which happened one row earlier, in 2016.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
stimulus: A comet's tail forms when sunlight and the solar wind push gas and dust away from its nucleus. Both forces are strongest at perihelion, the comet's closest approach to the Sun. However, heat takes time to reach a comet's buried ice. Astronomer Leandro Vey therefore predicted that the tail of comet C/2031 K4 would reach its greatest length only after perihelion. His measurements bear this out: the tail was longest ______ days after perihelion.

figure.caption: Tail Length of Comet C/2031 K4
figure.alt: Line graph of the comet's tail length in millions of kilometers, measured every 5 days from perihelion to 25 days after perihelion.

explanation: Find the highest point on the line, at 16 million kilometers. Then read straight down to the horizontal axis. That point sits at 10 days after perihelion.

A.why: Day 0 is perihelion itself. On that day the tail was at its shortest, 6 million kilometers, and the passage says the measurements showed the peak came after perihelion.

C.why: You read the point next to the peak. At 15 days the tail had already shrunk to 14 million kilometers.

D.why: 16 is the peak's value on the vertical axis, in millions of kilometers. The statement asks how many days after perihelion the peak occurred, which you read from the horizontal axis.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
stimulus:
Average Streamflow on the Teller River (cubic meters per second)
Month | Above reservoir | Below dam
February | 40 | 48
April | 120 | 80
June | 90 | 70
August | 25 | 50
October | 35 | 45

Hydrologist Amara Djalo compared streamflow at two gauges on the Teller River over the same year. One gauge was above Fenwick Reservoir and the other directly below its dam. The dam stores spring meltwater and releases it gradually. As a result, Djalo argues, flow below the dam does not drop as sharply in late summer as flow above the reservoir does. Even so, the gauge below the dam recorded its lowest monthly flow in ______.
explanation: The statement is about the gauge below the dam, so use only the "Below dam" column. Its smallest value is 45 cubic meters per second, in the October row.

A.why: You chose a nearby value that looked smallest. February's 48 is slightly higher than October's 45, so February is not the lowest month below the dam.

B.why: You reversed the comparison. April has the highest flow below the dam, 80 cubic meters per second, not the lowest.

C.why: You read the "Above reservoir" column, where August's 25 is the lowest value. Below the dam, August's flow was 50, one of the higher readings.
